title: The God of Mercy Will Indulge
description: The God of Mercy Will Indulge in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Fawcett wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 595 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Death of Parents”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The God of mer-cy will in-dulge The flow-ing tear, the heav-ing sigh, When hon-ored par-ents fall a-round, When friends be-loved and kin-dred die.

lines: The God of mercy will indulge
The flowing tear, the heaving sigh,
When friends beloved and kindred die.
Yet not one anxious, murmuring thought
Should with our mourning passions blend;
Nor should our bleeding hearts forget
Thou art each tender name in one;
On thee we cast our every care,
And comfort seek from thee alone.
To thee, our Father, would we look,
Our Rock, our Portion, and our Friend,
And on thy gracious love and truth

licence: Public domain: John Fawcett died in 1817.
credits: Words by John Fawcett (1740–1817), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
